subject: MerchantPrime: hot-path affinity & SLA gating — prioritize for close
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood-inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Alex Turner <a.turner@merchantprime.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantPrime: hot-path affinity & SLA gating — prioritize for close

Team — looping you in on an ask from MerchantPrime (re: MP-2026-045). They signed verbal LOI; procurement is asking for a delivery milestone that requires a small but non-trivial runtime feature set to be available in our next sprint. High level: they need (A) a tenant-level "hot-path" affinity flag that pins requests to a warmed KV/batch lane for a subset of traffic, (B) an SLA gating control so we can enforce a 99th pct latency target for tagged traffic with fallback to a lower-cost model, and (C) a per-session audit log export for compliance.

Why this matters: MerchantPrime is committing to a 12-month committed spend (>$1.2M ARR) if we can meet the pilot needs by Aug 1 and provide the gating/affinity guarantees in pilot. Marketing and legal are prepared to move fast but they need a clear engineering cut and timeline to finalize SOW.

Attachments: merchantprime-requirements-map.pdf (visual priority map), MP-2026-045-deal-summary.pdf (commercial terms).

Asks: 1) Maya/Prod — can we slot a scoped MVP for the affinity + basic gating controls in the sprint starting Jul 12? 2) Jonas/Eng — rough engineering effort (S, M, L) and blockers? 3) All — any obvious risk to other customers if we enable tenant pinning?

I know this is a tight timeline; appreciate candid tradeoffs. Can we triage this today and escalate if needed?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MerchantPrime: hot-path affinity & SLA gating — prioritize for close

On Sat, Jun 26, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> Team — looping you in on an ask from MerchantPrime (re: MP-2026-045). They signed verbal LOI; procurement is asking for a delivery milestone that requires a small but non-trivial runtime feature set to be available in our next sprint.

Thanks for the context. A few clarifying Qs before we commit sprint capacity: 
- Do they require hard latency SLAs with financial penalties, or an operational SLA for pilot observability? (different level of effort)
- For "hot-path" affinity, is the ask strictly a routing tag + pinned warm cache, or do they expect kernel-level priority preemption for their tenant?
- For the audit export: acceptable formats and retention windows? Will they want continuous streaming to their S3 or batched nightlies?

My initial thought: we can scope an MVP that exposes a tenant flag which opts traffic into an affinity profile (warmed cache + higher batching priority up to a configured cap). That avoids kernel preemption and keeps risk lower. For SLA gating we can provide a routing policy that sends overflow to a compatible, lower-cost model with explicit telemetry. This would be implementable as a config + policy change and a small runtime switch. 

Link to suggested spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-merchantprime-matrix (please add comments).

If Procurement is pushing for a hard SLA with penalties, we should loop Legal + Infra SRE to sign off. Otherwise I think Product can support an MVP for Jul 12 sprint if Eng confirms capacity.

-Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantPrime: hot-path affinity & SLA gating — prioritize for close

Thanks — quick engineering read: 
- Feasibility: tenant-level affinity flag + warmed KV cache lanes = feasible. We already have continuous-batching and per-tenant cache buckets; exposing a "hot-path" profile should be ~2-3 dev-weeks of work to wire config, tests, and a safe rollout path (canary + feature flag).
- SLA gating: implementing a routing policy that falls back to a compatible variant is low-risk (~1 dev-week) but *guaranteed* hard SLAs with penalties are not something we can promise without capacity reservations and SRE runbook (+SLA monitoring). That is a separate dedicated-capacity + SRE effort.
- Audit export: we can add per-session audit exports to the telemetry pipeline; streaming to customer S3 is straightforward but requires credentials + retention/legal signoff. Estimated 1 week.

Risks: warm-cache pinning increases memory pressure on GPU nodes; we need to cap the number of pinned tenants concurrently. If MerchantPrime expects a large proportion of traffic pinned, that becomes an Ops/Capacity discussion. 

Proposed a conservative rollout: (A) Build the config + affinity toggle as MVP (2-3w), (B) Expose SLA gating via routing policy (1w), (C) Audit export (1w). Total ~4-5 dev-weeks, with ability to parallelize some tasks if we prioritize. I'll attach a short sketch.

Attachment: eng-implementation-sketch.md

-Jonas

Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: MerchantPrime: hot-path affinity & SLA gating — prioritize for close

Thanks everyone — helpful and pragmatic takes. To summarize and make a call: 
- Product will scope an MVP that exposes a tenant "hot-path" flag (warmed cache + routing priority cap) and an SLA-gating routing policy (no financial SLA in MVP).
- Eng estimates ~4-5 dev-weeks total; with parallel work we can aim for a Jul 12 sprint kickoff to deliver a canary by Jul 30.
- Audit export to MerchantPrime S3 is OK pending credentials + legal signoff on retention (Marissa to lead).

Next steps: 
1) Ben — confirm MerchantPrime is OK with an operational SLA (observability & routing fallback) for pilot rather than a penalty-backed financial SLA. Please get confirmation by EOD Mon Jun 28.
2) Marissa — start procurement/legal checklist for S3 credentials and retention policy.
3) Jonas — open a lightweight RFC and ACs this week; mark any capacity gating limits we need.
4) Priyom/Maya — we'll block sprint capacity if Engineering confirms schedule by Tue Jun 29.

Ben — can you schedule a 30-min sync with MerchantPrime + Prod + Eng early next week? I'll host.

-Maya
